cases.sentence: Долли уже хотела ложиться, когда ___ в ночном костюме вошла к ней.
cases.translation: Dolly was about to go to bed when Anna, in her nightgown, came in to her.
cases.explain: Анна is the grammatical subject of вошла (came in), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Она сидела у ___, глядя на Долли и перебирая в памяти все те, казавшиеся неистощимыми, запасы задушевных разговоров, и не находила ничего.
cases.translation: She sat by the window, looking at Dolly and searching her memory for those seemingly inexhaustible stores of heartfelt conversation, and found nothing.
cases.explain: The preposition у (by/near) governs the genitive case, giving окна.

cases.sentence: По самому своему ___ они будут поставлены в необходимость стыдиться матери, отца, своего рождения.
cases.translation: By their very birth they will be forced to be ashamed of their mother, their father, their own birth.
cases.explain: The preposition по (by virtue of) governs the dative case, giving рождению.

cases.sentence: Анна заметила этот ___, выказывавший несогласие, и продолжала.
cases.translation: Anna noticed this sigh, which expressed disagreement, and continued.
cases.explain: Вздох is the direct object of the transitive verb заметила (noticed), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.translation: She stretched out her white hands in front of her belly.
cases.explain: The preposition пред (before, in front of) governs the instrumental case, giving животом.

cases.sentence: Понимаешь, что я не могу этого желать в моем ___.
cases.translation: You understand that I cannot wish for that in my situation.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) governs the prepositional case, giving положении.

reading.ru: Долли уже хотела ложиться, когда Анна в ночном костюме вошла к ней.
reading.question: What was Dolly about to do when Anna came to see her?
reading.explain: Dolly was about to go to bed when Anna, in her nightgown, came in to her.

reading.ru: Она сидела у окна, глядя на Долли и перебирая в памяти все те, казавшиеся неистощимыми, запасы задушевных разговоров, и не находила ничего.
reading.question: What happened to Anna when she tried to recall all the heartfelt things she wanted to say?
options: She sat by the window and found she had nothing to say
She recalled everything perfectly and spoke at length
reading.correct: She sat by the window and found she had nothing to say
reading.explain: Sitting by the window, searching her memory for the seemingly endless store of heartfelt talk, Anna found nothing to say.

reading.ru: Но ты знаешь, это не прощается».
reading.question: What does Anna say Kitty cannot forgive?
options: Anna's affair, which is unforgivable to Kitty
reading.correct: Anna's affair, which is unforgivable to Kitty
reading.explain: Anna acknowledges that what she did is something that cannot be forgiven by Kitty.

reading.question: How does Dolly describe Kitty's husband, Levin?
options: Calling him wonderful is an understatement
As a difficult and cold man
reading.correct: Calling him wonderful is an understatement
reading.explain: Dolly says it is an understatement to merely call Levin wonderful.

reading.ru: Ей было неловко называть его графом и Алексеем Кирилловичем.
reading.question: Why was Dolly uncomfortable when referring to Vronsky?
options: She found it awkward to call him either 'count' or 'Alexei Kirillovich'
She thought he did not deserve a title
She preferred to call him by a nickname
reading.correct: She found it awkward to call him either 'count' or 'Alexei Kirillovich'
reading.explain: The text says Dolly felt awkward calling him 'count' or 'Alexei Kirillovich.'

reading.ru: Но мы приехали раннюю весной, жили совершенно одни и будем жить одни.
reading.question: How does Anna describe her and Vronsky's life together, apart from summer visitors?
options: They came in early spring, lived completely alone, and will continue to live alone
They are constantly surrounded by guests
They plan to move to Petersburg soon
reading.correct: They came in early spring, lived completely alone, and will continue to live alone
reading.explain: Anna explains that they arrived in early spring and have lived, and will continue to live, entirely alone.

reading.question: Why is Vronsky away that day, according to Anna?
options: There are races that day and his horses are running
He is negotiating a business deal
reading.correct: There are races that day and his horses are running
reading.explain: Anna explains that today there are races, and his horses are running in them.

reading.ru: Ты знаешь, как я смотрю, но все-таки, если возможно, надо выйти замуж».
reading.question: What does Dolly advise Anna to do, if possible?
options: To marry, if it becomes possible
To give up the hospital project
reading.correct: To marry, if it becomes possible
reading.explain: Dolly says that despite her own views, Anna should try to marry if it is at all possible.

reading.ru: Она была в связи с Тушкевичем, самым гадким образом обманывая мужа.
reading.question: What does Anna say about Betsy Tverskaya's relationship with Tushkevich?
options: She was having an affair with him while deceiving her husband in the vilest way
She refused to speak to him at all
She helped him become a judge
reading.correct: She was having an affair with him while deceiving her husband in the vilest way
reading.explain: Anna recalls that Betsy was involved with Tushkevich, deceiving her husband in the most despicable manner.

reading.ru: Ему хочется, во-первых, узаконить свою дочь и быть твоим мужем, иметь право на тебя».
reading.question: What does Vronsky want, according to what he told Dolly?
options: To legitimize his daughter and become Anna's legal husband
To leave Anna and remarry someone else
To send his daughter away to relatives
To give up his estate to Anna
reading.correct: To legitimize his daughter and become Anna's legal husband
reading.explain: Vronsky wants first of all to legitimize his daughter and to become Anna's husband, having a right to her.

reading.ru: У меня не будет больше детей».
reading.question: What does Anna declare about having more children?
options: That she will not have any more children
That she wants many more children
That the decision is entirely up to Vronsky
That she is already pregnant again
reading.correct: That she will not have any more children
reading.explain: Anna states plainly that she will not have any more children.

reading.question: What does Anna say a doctor told her after her illness?
options: Something that made her sure she would not have more children
That she needed to move to a warmer climate
That she should never travel again
reading.correct: Something that made her sure she would not have more children
reading.explain: Anna explains that a doctor told her something after her illness, implying she will not have more children.

reading.ru: Она чувствовала, что это было слишком простое решение слишком сложного вопроса.
reading.question: How did Dolly feel about Anna's method of avoiding pregnancy?
options: That it was too simple a solution to too complex a question
That it was a perfectly reasonable decision
That it was something she wished she had known earlier
That it did not concern her at all
reading.correct: That it was too simple a solution to too complex a question
reading.explain: The text says Dolly felt this was too simple a solution to too complicated a question.

reading.ru: Или быть беременной, то есть больною, или быть другом, товарищем своего мужа.
reading.question: What choice does Anna say she faces?
options: Either being pregnant (that is, ill) or being her husband's friend and companion
Either staying in the countryside or moving to the city
Either loving Sergei or loving Annie
reading.correct: Either being pregnant (that is, ill) or being her husband's friend and companion
reading.explain: Anna says her choice is between being pregnant, meaning ill, or being a friend and companion to her husband.

reading.ru: Она вытянула белые руки пред животом.
reading.question: What gesture did Anna make while speaking of keeping Vronsky's love?
options: She stretched out her white hands in front of her body
She covered her face with her hands
She clenched her fists in anger
She reached out to hold Dolly's hand
reading.correct: She stretched out her white hands in front of her body
reading.explain: The text says Anna stretched her white hands out in front of her body as she spoke.

reading.ru: Если он будет искать этого, то найдет туалеты и манеры еще более привлекательные и веселые.
reading.question: What did Dolly fear a man like Vronsky could always find elsewhere?
options: Even more attractive and cheerful looks and manners
reading.correct: Even more attractive and cheerful looks and manners
reading.explain: Dolly reflects that if he looked for it, he would always find toilettes and manners even more attractive and cheerful.

reading.ru: По самому своему рождению они будут поставлены в необходимость стыдиться матери, отца, своего рождения.
reading.question: What does Dolly say illegitimate children would be forced to feel?
options: Shame about their mother, father, and their own birth
reading.correct: Shame about their mother, father, and their own birth
reading.explain: Dolly argues that by their very birth, such children would be forced to feel ashamed of their mother, father, and their own birth.

reading.ru: Могло ли быть в каком-нибудь случае лучше для ее любимца Гриши, если бы он никогда не существовал?
reading.question: What strange thought occurred to Dolly about her son Grisha?
options: Whether it could ever have been better for him if he had never existed
Whether he resembled his father too much
Whether he needed a new tutor
reading.correct: Whether it could ever have been better for him if he had never existed
reading.explain: Dolly suddenly wonders whether it could in any case have been better for her beloved Grisha if he had never existed.

reading.ru: Она вдруг почувствовала, что стала уж так далека от Анны, что между ними существуют вопросы, в которых они никогда не сойдутся и о которых лучше не говорить.
reading.question: What did Dolly realize about her relationship with Anna by the end of their talk?
options: That she had become so distant from Anna that some questions were better left undiscussed
That she and Anna agreed on everything
That she wanted to move in with Anna permanently
That Anna no longer trusted her at all
reading.correct: That she had become so distant from Anna that some questions were better left undiscussed
reading.explain: Dolly suddenly felt she had become so distant from Anna that there existed questions on which they would never agree and which were better left unspoken.

highlight.question: Which sentence indicates that Anna has important personal matters she wants to discuss with Dolly in private?
sentences: В продолжение дня несколько раз Анна начинала разговоры о задушевных делах и каждый раз, сказав несколько слов, останавливалась.
«После, наедине все переговорим.
Мне столько тебе нужно сказать», – говорила она.
highlight.explain: Anna emphasizes that she will talk everything over later when they are alone, indicating significant matters requiring privacy.

highlight.question: Which sentence shows Anna's main defense when Dolly confronts her about her relationship with Stiva?
sentences: – Да, да, – отвернувшись и глядя в открытое окно, сказала Анна.
– Но я не была виновата.
И кто виноват?
Что такое виноват?
Разве могло быть иначе?
Ну, как ты думаешь?
Могло ли быть, чтобы ты не была жена Стивы?
highlight.explain: Anna insists that she was not the one at fault, establishing her position before questioning the meaning of guilt itself.

highlight.question: Which sentence asks Dolly to truly understand Anna's difficult position and personal suffering?
sentences: – Разумеется, – перебила она Долли, хотевшую возразить, – разумеется, я насильно не удержу его.
Я и не держу.
Нынче скачки, его лошади скачут, он едет.
Но ты подумай обо мне, представь себе мое положение…
Да что говорить про это!
– Она улыбнулась.
– Так о чем же он говорил с тобой?
highlight.explain: Anna appeals to Dolly to imagine what she is experiencing, emphasizing the need for empathy about her situation.

highlight.question: Which sentence characterizes Stiva's desires as legitimate and noble despite being selfish?
sentences: – Он сказал, что страдает за тебя и за себя.
Может быть, ты скажешь, что это эгоизм, но такой законный и благородный эгоизм!
Ему хочется, во-первых, узаконить свою дочь и быть твоим мужем, иметь право на тебя.
highlight.explain: Anna frames Stiva's egoism as lawful and honorable, suggesting that his motives are understandable even if self-serving.

highlight.question: Which sentence expresses Anna's deepest insecurity about the permanence of her relationship?
sentences: – Для тебя, для других, – говорила Анна, как будто угадывая ее мысли, – еще может быть сомнение; но для меня…
Ты пойми, я не жена; он любит меня до тех пор, пока любит.
И что ж, чем же я поддержу его любовь?
highlight.explain: Anna reveals her fear that she is not truly a wife and that Stiva's love depends entirely on his continuing feelings for her.

highlight.question: Which sentence reveals that Anna's greatest concern about motherhood is the social status of any children she might have?
sentences: Но надо рассудить, – продолжала она.
– Ты забываешь мое положение.
Как я могу желать детей?
Я не говорю про страдания, я их не боюсь.
Подумай, кто будут мои дети?
highlight.explain: Anna's question about who her children would be points to her fear of bringing illegitimate children into an impossible situation.
